??? question "Which pair of nearly identical test programs shows that a rule is enforced exactly where it should be?"

    A valid and invalid pair, one accepted and one rejected.

    Introduced in [11. Release](stage-11-release.md).

??? question "Which written record does a test compare against to decide whether it passed?"

    The expected output, such as the program's printed text or the error's kind and location.

    Introduced in [0. The workbench](stage-0-workbench.md).

??? question "What is a named version of the compiler, offered to others as working with its limits stated, called?"

    A release.

    Introduced in [11. Release](stage-11-release.md).

??? question "Which planned type would view part of an array with a length known only at run time, and what do you use in v0.1 instead?"

    A slice, such as `&[f32]`. In v0.1 you use a reference to a fixed-size array, such as `&[f32; 4]`.

    Introduced in [Learn: 9. Planned types](../../language-tour/05-types-planned-for-later.md).

??? question "What do we call code written in the most direct way, with no attempt to make it fast?"

    Naive, like the straightforward, unoptimized v0.1 matrix multiplication.

    Introduced in [10. Matrix multiplication](stage-10-matrix-multiplication.md).

??? question "Which half of the compiler reads the source, works out what it means and rejects bad programs?"

    The front end. In this guide it is stages 1 to 5.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "Which kind of test runs the whole compiler on a source file, runs the result and checks what comes out?"

    An end-to-end test.

    Introduced in [11. Release](stage-11-release.md).

??? question "What do we call a matrix with as many rows as columns?"

    A square matrix, such as 4 by 4.

    Introduced in [10. Matrix multiplication](stage-10-matrix-multiplication.md).

??? question "What do we call something the language describes that this compiler does not yet do, written down for users?"

    A known limitation.

    Introduced in [11. Release](stage-11-release.md).

??? question "What is a fresh copy of the project's files, with nothing left over from earlier builds, called?"

    A clean checkout.

    Introduced in [11. Release](stage-11-release.md).

??? question "What do we call loops placed inside other loops, such as the three loops of matrix multiplication?"

    A loop nest.

    Introduced in [10. Matrix multiplication](stage-10-matrix-multiplication.md).

??? question "To multiply A by B, which size must match, and what is it called?"

    The inner dimension, the number of columns of A, which must equal the number of rows of B.

    Introduced in [10. Matrix multiplication](stage-10-matrix-multiplication.md).

??? question "What do we call one small, automatic check with a definite pass or fail answer?"

    A test. It either passes or fails, with nothing in between.

    Introduced in [0. The workbench](stage-0-workbench.md).

??? question "What do we call one trip over the whole program by one part of the compiler, doing one job?"

    A pass, such as checking types or lowering to IR.

    Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

??? question "What is a result worked out independently, by hand or by trusted software, that a test compares the output against?"

    A known answer.

    Introduced in [10. Matrix multiplication](stage-10-matrix-multiplication.md).

??? question "What is a rectangle of numbers in rows and columns called, and how is it written in v0.1?"

    A matrix. In v0.1 it is simply a two-dimensional array such as `[f32; 2, 3]`.

    Introduced in [10. Matrix multiplication](stage-10-matrix-multiplication.md).

??? question "What is the whole collection of automated tests for the compiler called?"

    The test suite.

    Introduced in [11. Release](stage-11-release.md).

??? question "What do we call a matrix whose numbers of rows and columns differ, such as 2 by 3?"

    A rectangular matrix.

    Introduced in [10. Matrix multiplication](stage-10-matrix-multiplication.md).

??? question "What do we call multiplying two equal-length lists position by position and adding up the results?"

    A dot product. Each cell of a matrix product is one.

    Introduced in [10. Matrix multiplication](stage-10-matrix-multiplication.md).

??? question "What do we call a program that reads source code, checks it, and writes out code a machine can run?"

    A compiler. It also rejects programs that break the rules and explains the problem.

    Introduced in [Overview](index.md).

??? question "What lets people say exactly which release of the compiler they used, such as `v0.1.0`?"

    The version number.

    Introduced in [11. Release](stage-11-release.md).

??? question "In a matrix, what are one horizontal line and one vertical line called, and how many of each does a 2 by 3 matrix have?"

    A row and a column. A 2 by 3 matrix has 2 rows and 3 columns.

    Introduced in [10. Matrix multiplication](stage-10-matrix-multiplication.md).

??? question "What is a test that is known to fail, and marked that way on purpose, called?"

    An expected failure, usually a test of a known limitation.

    Introduced in [11. Release](stage-11-release.md).

??? question "Which operation builds each cell of a matrix C from one row of A and one column of B?"

    Matrix multiplication. Each cell of the result is one dot product.

    Introduced in [10. Matrix multiplication](stage-10-matrix-multiplication.md).

??? question "When a test compares floating-point results, what says how far apart they may be and still count as equal?"

    The tolerance.

    Introduced in [10. Matrix multiplication](stage-10-matrix-multiplication.md).

??? question "What do we call a point where a compiler supports less than the language allows, such as a maximum array size?"

    An implementation limit. The specification requires it to be documented.

    Introduced in [11. Release](stage-11-release.md). Specification: [1. Conformance and terminology](../../specification/conformance.md#13-implementation-conformance).

??? question "What is the list of checks that must all pass before a release may be named?"

    The release gate.

    Introduced in [11. Release](stage-11-release.md).

??? question "What is the full description of a value's size, alignment and the offset of each of its parts called?"

    Its layout.

    Introduced in [8. Data in memory](stage-8-data-in-memory.md). Specification: [8. Structs](../../specification/structs.md#88-layout).
